A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same TFM-Tokenizer study with complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison; all appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: V4 reports original TFM-Tokenizer evaluations on clinical EEG and ear-EEG tasks in Tables 1–3, plus ablations, token analyses and cross-dataset experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V5 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, token analyses and cross-dataset experiments in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same dual-path encoding, vector-quantized vocabulary, masking objectives, downstream training and BIOT/LaBraM integration procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TUEV, TUAB, IIIC Seizure, CHB-MIT and EESM23. The clinical classification tasks, cross-dataset scenarios and ear-EEG sleep-staging evaluation are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and 9 and the tokenizer analyses, including the BIOT and LaBraM comparisons. The newly cited motif-learning studies are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same pretraining settings, data splits, preprocessing, evaluation metrics and ear-EEG fine-tuning protocol. Model configurations and experimental budgets in Appendix D also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.5–4.7 and Appendix C retain the same component and masking ablations, token-quality analyses, cross-dataset tests, vocabulary/window-size studies and qualitative motif examples.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 specifies five random seeds and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting in both versions. Uncertainty displays and the ear-EEG comparison's reported p = 0.02 are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains the multi-dataset TUEV Cohen's kappa of 0.6189 ± 0.0302 for TFM-Tokenizer.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same STFT definition, tokenization and classification formulations, quantization rule and training objectives. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning single-channel motif tokenization, accuracy, foundation-model integration and cross-device scalability. The specific time-frequency tokenization novelty claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of joint time-frequency learning, token quality and generalization remain unchanged. Sections 4.6–4.7 retain the qualifications about retrieval metrics and fixed windows splitting larger motifs or shifted patterns.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement and Appendices B, D and E provide identical preprocessing, hyperparameter, tuning and integration details. Code and pretrained-weight access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the description of EEG motif learning as largely underexplored with acknowledgment of several prior studies. It adds Mueen et al. (2009), Barthélemy et al. (2013), Gips et al. (2017) and Jas et al. (2017), while retaining the temporal-domain distinction and specific novelty claim.

P1.justification: V5 locally revises the motif-related-work paragraph, identifies corresponding authors, adds a funding acknowledgment and makes the reproducibility heading unnumbered. It also corrects the Vaswani author attribution; the overall narrative and appendix structure remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 4 and 5 receive small cropping or scaling adjustments without changing their content. Table 3 changes the LaBraM-TFM weighted F1 entry, 0.4864 ± 0.0118, from red to black. Author-block formatting and reference pagination also change.

improvement.justification: V5 modestly improves scholarly context by replacing Section 2's largely-underexplored framing with explicit recognition of four additional prior motif-learning studies. This improves attribution and research positioning while preserving the scientific content and evidence. The author, funding and formatting updates provide smaller supporting benefits.
